counterfactual_missing_items: The lesions followed the course of branches of the common plantar digital nerves without evidence of invasion.
On T2-weighted fat-suppressed images, they were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration; each was surrounded by a hyperintense rim.
She denied any trauma and had no family history of neurofibromatosis
decisive_items: On T2-weighted fat-suppressed images, they were homogeneously hyperintense without cystic degeneration; each was surrounded by a hyperintense rim.
A small extension of high signal from the lateral aspect of one lesion resembled a “mouse-tail.”
response.rationale: R2 uniquely ties together the linearly distributed multiple nodules along plantar digital nerves with the MRI features of homogeneous T2 hyperintensity, hyperintense rims, and a mouse-tail sign, and it matches the explicitly suspected diagnosis. R3 shares the nerve-course anatomy but lacks the specific schwannoma imaging pattern and is weakened by the absent neurofibromatosis family history. R1 explains the cold/compression/nocturnal pain but does not account for the multi-nodular nerve-distribution imaging findings or the mouse-tail sign.

rejected.why: The clinical pain features are compatible with glomus tumor, but the linear multi-nodular distribution along plantar digital nerves, T2 hyperintense rims, and mouse-tail sign are much more specific for a peripheral nerve sheath tumor, favoring plexiform schwannoma.
